# Microsoft Purview deployment models
 Feedback
 Summarize this article for me
## 
Microsoft Purview provides integrated solutions and features that complement each other. For new Microsoft Purview administrators, it can be overwhelming to know where to start. But even existing administrators might be unfamiliar with how some Micro
To address the need for shorter, actionable, and prescriptive guidance, the Product Engineering team is releasing a new series: Microsoft Purview Deployment Models. Deployment models are scenario-based and include a comprehensive step-by-step guide t
## Audience
IT professionals, security professionals, and compliance officers who are responsible for deploying and managing Microsoft Purview in their organization. They don't provide detailed technical guidance but rather a high-level overview of the deploymen
Deployment models come from our engineering teams. They're based on proven deployments with organizations. The objective of deployment models is to enable organizations to accelerate securing content and deploy faster.
## Secure by default with Microsoft Purview
Use this deployment model to help rapidly implement a secure by default configuration with Microsoft Purview Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention, and Insider Risk Management.
- Introduction
- Step 1: Start with default labeling
- Step 2: Address files with the highest sensitivity
- Step 3: Expand protection to your entire Microsoft 365 data estate
- Step 4: Operate, expand, and retroactive actions
## Prevent data leak to shadow AI
Use this deployment model to help your organization identify and prevent data leaks to shadow AI by using Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Intune.
- Introduction
- Step 1: Discover AI apps
- Step 2: Block access to unsanctioned AI apps
- Step 3: Block sensitive data going to sanctioned AI apps
- Step 4: Govern data sent to AI apps
## Secure and govern Microsoft 365 Copilot agents
Use this deployment model for Microsoft 365 Copilot agents by securing both the grounding data and interactions with Microsoft Purview.
- Introduction
- Step 1: Discover risks and identify gaps
- Step 2: Protect sensitive info in grounding data
- Step 3: Protect interactions
- Step 4: Govern interactions
## Deploy and use Data Security Posture Management
Use this deployment model to prepare for a Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) deployment with step-by-step guidance.
- Introduction
- Step 1: Establish foundational elements
- Step 2: Configure access and analytics
- Step 3: Understand data landscape and risks
- Step 4: Take action and investigate with Security Copilot
## Lightweight guide to mitigate data leakage
Use this deployment model to enable core data security capabilities with minimal configuration, focusing on essential steps to get started quickly.
- Introduction
- Step 1: Establish foundational data security
- Step 2: Expand protection to endpoints
- Step 3: Continuous improvement
## Reduce false positives by using SITs and advanced classifiers
Use this deployment model to minimize false positives by effectively leveraging the classification capabilities of Microsoft Purview.

## Turn on data security prerequisites and advanced analytics
Microsoft Purview has many capabilities. To reduce impacts to users, some capabilities aren't activated by default. Review the following settings:
- Turn on ability to process content in Office Online: Enable sensitivity labels for files in SharePoint and OneDrive
- Turn on labeling for Microsoft Teams and SharePoint Sites: Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites)
- Keep the label mismatch email label. This feature sends an email to the document owner and site owner about a document that has a higher sensitivity than the site’s sensitivity label. You can confirm it's not disabled by verifying -BlockSendLabelMismatchEmail is set to $False.
- Include a help link with -LabelMismatchEmailHelpLink.
- Enable support for PDF files in OneDrive and SharePoint: Enable sensitivity labels for files in SharePoint and OneDrive
- Mark files as sensitive by default: Prevent guest access to files while DLP rules are applied - SharePoint in Microsoft 365
- DLP analytics: Get started with data loss prevention analytics
- Turn on co-authoring for files with sensitivity labels: Enable co-authoring for encrypted documents
- Insider Risk Management analytics: Enable analytics in Insider Risk Management
- Turn on Insider Risk Management Indicators: Configure policy indicators in insider risk management
- Turn on Microsoft Purview audits: Get started with auditing solutions
- Enable integration with Microsoft Entra B2B: SharePoint and OneDrive integration with Microsoft Entra B2B

content.content:
## Discover and monitor AI app usage with Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Use Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps to discover and monitor AI app usage across your organization. Defender for Cloud Apps provides a risk assessment for each discovered app to help you determine whether to sanction or unsanction an app.
- Filter the Cloud app catalog by App category > Generative AI to identify AI apps in use.
- Review the risk score and usage details for each discovered AI app.
- Tag apps as Sanctioned or Unsanctioned based on your organization's policy.
Tip
Use the cloud discovery dashboard to identify AI app usage trends before making sanctioning decisions. Understanding the scope of AI app usage helps you prioritize which apps to address first.
## Discover user interactions with Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI
## Block pasting and uploading of sensitive info with Endpoint DLP
Use Microsoft Purview Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to block pasting and uploading of sensitive information to AI apps. Endpoint DLP monitors user activities on managed devices and can prevent sensitive data from being shared through copy/paste operations or file uploads to AI application websites.
- Create a DLP policy with Devices as the location.
- Set conditions to detect content containing sensitive information types or sensitivity labels.
- Set actions to block paste to browser, upload to cloud services, or copy to clipboard for AI application websites.
- Run in simulation mode first to understand the impact on users.
Tip
Review the DLP activity explorer to identify false positives and fine-tune your policy conditions.
## Block sensitive info in AI prompts in Microsoft Edge
Use Microsoft Purview DLP or collection policies for Microsoft Edge to block sensitive information in text prompts being sent to consumer AI applications, including ChatGPT (consumer), Microsoft Copilot (consumer version), DeepSeek, and Google Gemini.
Browser Data Security in Microsoft Edge enables DLP policies to inspect text that users type or paste into AI application prompts in real time, blocking the submission of sensitive content before it leaves the browser.
To learn more, see Learn about Browser Data Security.
## Detect sensitive data shared through non-Microsoft browsers and apps

A successful strategy to deploy sensitivity labels for an organization is to create a working virtual team that identifies and manages the business and technical requirements, proof of concept testing, internal checkpoints and approvals, and final deployment for the production environment.
Using the table in the next section, we recommend identifying your top one or two scenarios that map to your most impactful business requirements. After these scenarios are deployed, return to the list to identify the next one or two priorities for deployment.
Tip
To help accelerate your deployment, use the Overview page from Information Protection in the Microsoft Purview portal to see labeling recommendations and reports specific to your organization, and more.

## Requirements
These new capabilities work with sensitivity labels only.
Use the OneDrive sync app version 19.002.0121.0008 or later on Windows, and version 19.002.0107.0008 or later on macOS. Both these versions were released January 28, 2019. For more information, see the OneDrive release notes. After you enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive, users who run an older version of the sync app see a prompt
## Supported file types
## SharePoint Information Rights Management (IRM) and sensitivity labels
SharePoint Information Rights Management (IRM) is an older technology to protect files at the list and library level by applying encryption and restrictions when users download files. This older protection technology is designed to prevent unauthorized users from opening the file while it's outside SharePoint.
In comparison, sensitivity labels provide the protection settings of visual markings (headers, footers, watermarks) in addition to encryption. The encryption settings support the full range of usage rights to restrict what users can do with the content, and the same sensitivity labels are supported for many scenarios. Using the same protection method with consistent settings across workloads and a
However, you can use both protection solutions together and the behavior is as follows:
- 
If you upload a file with a sensitivity label that applies encryption, SharePoint can't process the content of these files so coauthoring, eDiscovery, DLP, and search aren't supported for these files.
- 
If you label a file using Office for the web, any encryption settings from the label are enforced. For these files, coauthoring, eDiscovery, DLP, and search are supported.
- 
If you download a file that's labeled by using Office for the web, the label is retained and any encryption settings from the label are enforced rather than the IRM restriction settings.
- 
If you download an Office or PDF file that isn't encrypted with a sensitivity label, IRM settings are applied.
- 
If you enabled any of the additional IRM library settings, which include preventing users from uploading documents that don't support IRM, these settings are enforced.
With this behavior, you can be assured that all Office and PDF files are protected from unauthorized access if they're downloaded, even if they aren't labeled. However, labeled files that are uploaded don't benefit from the new capabilities.
## Search for documents by sensitivity label
## Next steps
After you enable sensitivity labels for files in SharePoint and OneDrive, consider automatically labeling files by using either, or both, of the following labeling methods:
- Applying a default sensitivity label for document libraries, for new and edited files in SharePoint. For more information, see Configure a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library.
- Auto-labeling policies that use content inspection for files in SharePoint and OneDrive. For more information, see Automatically apply a sensitivity label to Microsoft 365 data.

# Enable sensitivity labels for files in SharePoint and OneDrive
Enable built-in labeling for supported Office files and PDF files in SharePoint and OneDrive so that users can apply your sensitivity labels in Office for the web. When this feature is enabled, users see the Sensitivity button on the ribbon so they can apply labels, and see any applied label name on the status bar.
Users can also see and apply sensitivity labels without having to first open the files, by using the details pane in SharePoint and OneDrive. This labeling method is also available from the Files tab in Microsoft Teams.
Enabling this feature also results in SharePoint and OneDrive being able to process the contents of Office files and optionally, PDF documents that have been encrypted by using a sensitivity label. The label can be applied in Office for the web, or in Office desktop apps and uploaded or saved in SharePoint and OneDrive. Until you enable this featur
After you enable sensitivity labels for these files in SharePoint and OneDrive, for new and changed files that have a sensitivity label that applies encryption with a cloud-based key (and doesn't use Double Key Encryption):
Use Office for the web (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) to open and edit Office files that have sensitivity labels that apply encryption. The permissions that were assigned with the encryption are enforced. You can also use auto-labeling for these documents.
eDiscovery supports full-text search for these files and data loss prevention (DLP) policies support content in these files.
If encryption has been applied with an on-premises key (a key management topology often referred to as "hold your own key" or HYOK), or by using Double Key Encryption, the service behavior for processing the file contents doesn't change. So for these files, coauthoring, eDiscovery, data loss prevention, search, and other collaborative features won'
The SharePoint and OneDrive behavior also doesn't change for existing files in these locations that are labeled with encryption using a single Azure-based key. For these files to benefit from the new capabilities after you enable sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive, the files must be either downloaded and uploaded again,

If you haven't yet enabled sensitivity labels for containers, do the following set of steps as a one-time procedure:

Because this feature uses Microsoft Entra functionality, follow the instructions from the Microsoft Entra documentation to enable sensitivity label support: Assign sensitivity labels to Microsoft 365 groups in Microsoft Entra ID.

You now need to synchronize your sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra ID. First, connect to Security & Compliance PowerShell.
For example, in a PowerShell session that you run as administrator, sign in with a global administrator account.
- 
Then run the following command to ensure your sensitivity labels can be used with Microsoft 365 groups:
Execute-AzureAdLabelSync

#### Planning for prerequisites
Before you can monitor some DLP locations, there are prerequisites that must be met. See the Before you begin sections of the following articles:
- Get started with the data loss prevention on-premises scanner
- Get started with Endpoint data loss prevention
- Get started with the Microsoft compliance extension
- Use data loss prevention policies for non-Microsoft cloud apps
#### Policy deployment
When you create your DLP policies, you should consider rolling them out gradually, so you can assess their impact and test their effectiveness before fully enforcing them. For example, you don't want a new DLP policy to unintentionally block access to thousands of documents or to break an existing business process.
If you're creating DLP policies with a large potential impact, we recommend following this sequence:
- 
Run the policy in simulation mode, without Policy Tips and then use the DLP reports, and any incident reports, to assess the impact of the policies. You can use DLP reports to view the number, location, type, and severity of policy matches. Based on the results, you can fine-tune your policies as needed. ## Step 1: Verify organization subscription and billing
Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool and per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records.
When a user or admin performs an audited activity, the system generates an audit record and stores it in the audit log for your organization. In Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium), you can retain and search audit records in the audit log for 180 days.
The default retention period for Audit (Standard) changed from 90 days to 180 days. Audit (Standard) logs that were generated before October 17, 2023, are retained for 90 days. Audit (Standard) logs that are generated on or after October 17, 2023, follow the new default retention of 180 days.
For a list of subscription and licensing requirements for these auditing solutions, see the subscription requirements for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium).
## Step 2: Assign permissions to search the audit log
## Step 3: Enable/Disable SearchQueryInitiatedExchange/SearchQueryInitiatedSharePoint events
Set-Mailbox <user> -AuditOwner @{Add="SearchQueryInitiated"} // For Exchange Online
Set-Mailbox <user> -AuditOwner @{Add="SharepointSearchQueryInitiated"} // For SharePoint. Enabled by default.
In a multi-geo environment, you must run the Set-Mailbox command in the forest where the user's mailbox is located. To identify the user's mailbox location, run the following cmdlet:
Get-Mailbox <user identity> | FL MailboxLocations
If you previously ran the cmdlet to enable auditing of search queries in a forest that's different than the forest where the user's mailbox is located, remove the SearchQueryInitiated/SharepointSearchQueryInitiated value from the user's mailbox. To remove the value, run Set-Mailbox -AuditOwner @{Rem
## Step 4: Set up Audit (Premium) for users
Organizations using Audit (Standard) can skip this step.
Audit (Premium) features, such as the ability to log intelligent insights, require an appropriate E5 license assigned to users. Additionally, you must enable the Advanced Auditing app/service plan for those users.
To enable the Advanced Auditing service plan for users, complete the following steps for each user:
- On the user properties flyout page, select Licenses and apps.
- In the Licenses section, verify that the user is assigned an E5 license or is assigned an appropriate add-on license. For a list of licenses that support Audit (Premium), see Audit licensing requirements.
- Select Save changes. The logging of Audit (Premium) insights begins within 24 hours.
If you customize the mailbox actions that are logged on user mailboxes or shared mailboxes, new Audit (Premium) events released by Microsoft aren't automatically audited on those mailboxes. For information about changing the mailbox actions that are audited for each sign-in type, see the "Change or 
## Step 5: Set up audit retention policies in Audit (Premium)
Organizations using Audit (Standard) can skip this step.
In addition to the default policy that retains Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive, and SharePoint audit records for one year, organizations using Audit (Premium) can create audit log retention policies to meet the requirements of your organization's security operations, IT, and compliance teams.
## Step 6: Search for audited events
Now that you have Audit (Standard) or Audit (Premium) configured for your organization, you're ready to search the audit log in the Microsoft Purview portal. For detailed guidance, see Search the audit log.

#### Prerequisites for accessing cloud indicators
To select from cloud indicators in Insider Risk Management settings and policies, you must first connect to the relevant cloud apps in Microsoft Defender, if you didn't already.
After connecting to the apps, you can find the indicators on the Policy indicators settings page and from individual policies.
### Configure Insider Risk Indicator (preview) connector
### Configure Microsoft 365 HR connector
Insider Risk Management supports importing user and log data imported from third-party risk management and human resources platforms. The Microsoft 365 Human Resources (HR) data connector allows you to pull in human resources data from CSV files, including user termination dates, last employment dates, performance improvement plan notifications, performance review actions, and 
The Microsoft 365 HR connector is required when using the following policy templates:
- Data leaks by risky users
- Departing user data theft
- Patient data misuse
- Security policy violations by departing users
- Security policy violations by risky users
For step-by-step guidance to configure the Microsoft 365 HR connector for your organization, see the Set up a connector to import HR data article. After you configure the HR connector, return to these configuration steps.
### Configure a Microsoft Healthcare connector
### Configure data loss prevention (DLP) policies
Insider Risk Management supports using DLP policies to help identify the intentional or accidental exposure of sensitive information to unwanted parties for high severity level DLP alerts. When you configure an Insider Risk Management policy with any of the Data leaks templates, you can assign a specific DLP policy to the policy for these types of alerts.
Tip
You can also use Adaptive Protection in Insider Risk Management to dynamically apply DLP protection controls to high-risk users while maintaining productivity for lower-risk users. Learn more about Adaptive Protection.
Data loss policies help identify users to activate risk scoring in Insider Risk Management for high severity DLP alerts for sensitive information. They're an important part of configuring full risk management coverage in your organization. For more information about Insider Risk Management and DLP policy integration and planning considerations, see Insider Risk Management polic
Important
Make sure you complete the following steps:
- Understand and properly configure the users included in both the DLP and Insider Risk Management policies to produce the policy coverage you expect.
- Configure the Incident reports setting in the DLP policy for Insider Risk Management used with these templates for High severity level alerts. Insider Risk Management alerts aren't generated from DLP policies with the Incident reports field set at Low or Medium.
A DLP policy is optional when using the following policy templates:
- Data leaks
- Data leaks by priority users
For step-by-step guidance to configure DLP policies for your organization, see Create and Deploy data loss prevention policies. After you configure a DLP policy, return to these configuration steps.
Note
Endpoint DLP now supports virtualized environments, which means that the Insider Risk Management solution supports virtualized environments through endpoint DLP. Learn more about support for virtualized environments in endpoint DLP.

### Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is an enterprise endpoint security platform designed to help enterprise networks prevent, detect, investigate, and respond to advanced threats. To gain better visibility of security violations in your organization, you can import and filter Defender for Endpoint alerts for activities used in policies created from Insider Risk Management security 
If you create security violation policies, you need to configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint in your organization and enable Defender for Endpoint for Insider Risk Management integration in the Defender Security Center to import security violation alerts. For more information about requirements, see the Minimum requirements for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint article.
For step-by-step guidance to configure Defender for Endpoint for Insider Risk Management integration, see the Configure advanced features in Defender for Endpoint article. After you configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, return to these configuration steps.

## Step 2 (required): Enable the Microsoft 365 audit log
Insider Risk Management uses Microsoft 365 audit logs for user insights and risk management activities identified in policies and analytics insights. The Microsoft 365 audit logs are a summary of all activities within your organization and Insider Risk Management policies might use these activities for generating policy insights
Auditing is enabled for Microsoft 365 organizations by default. Some organizations might have disabled auditing for specific reasons. If auditing is disabled for your organization, it might be because another administrator has turned it off. We recommend confirming that it's OK to turn auditing back on when completing this step.

## Step 3 (optional): Enable and view insider risk analytics insights
If you enable Insider Risk Management analytics, you can:
- Scan for potential insider risks before creating policies. You can conduct an evaluation of potential insider risks in your organization without configuring any insider risk policies. This evaluation can help your organization identify potential areas of higher user risk and help determine the type and scope of Insider Risk Ma
as reports for review. To learn more about analytics insights, see Insider Risk Management settings: Analytics and check out the Insider Risk Management Analytics video to help understand how analytics can help accelerate the identification of potential insider risks and help you to quickly take action.
- Receive real-time recommendations for indicator threshold settings. Manually tuning policies to reduce "noise" can be a very time-consuming experience that requires you to do a lot of trial and error to determine the desired configuration for your policies. If analytics is turned on, Insider Risk Management can provide real-ti
and see in real time how many users are brought into scope of the policy based on the changes you make. Learn more about real-time indicator threshold recommendations
Note
To enable insider risk analytics, you must be a member of the Insider Risk Management, Insider Risk Management Admins, or Microsoft 365 Global admin role group.

## Understand requirements and dependencies
Depending on how you plan to implement Insider Risk Management policies, you need the proper Microsoft 365 licensing subscriptions. You also need to understand and plan for some solution prerequisites.
Licensing: Microsoft offers Insider Risk Management as part of a wide selection of Microsoft 365 licensing subscriptions. For details, see the Getting started with Insider Risk Management article.
Important
Microsoft currently offers Insider Risk Management in tenants hosted in geographical country/regions supported by Azure service dependencies. To verify that Microsoft supports Insider Risk Management for your organization, see Azure dependency availability by country/region.
If you don't have an existing Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5 plan and want to try Insider Risk Management, you can add Microsoft 365 to your existing subscription or sign up for a trial of Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5.
Policy template requirements: Depending on the policy template you choose, understand the following requirements and plan accordingly prior to configuring Insider Risk Management in your organization:
- For the Data theft by departing users template, configure a Microsoft 365 HR connector to periodically import resignation and termination date information for users in your organization. For step-by-step guidance to configure the Microsoft 365 HR connector, see the Import data with the HR connector article.

**1a. Planning guide to move to Microsoft Intune.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/planning-guide (Intune, Entra P1/P2, MDE, Purview, M365 Apps)
- Order: Yes, 7 steps: objectives, inventory devices, costs and licensing, review existing policies and infrastructure, rollout plan, communicate, support help desk.
- Prerequisites: No (it is itself the prerequisite of Step 1).
- Dependencies: enforcing Intune compliance or password rules needs Entra ID P1/P2 as well as Intune. Blocking access by MDE threat level needs Conditional Access. Review GPOs and design groups before you build Intune policy.
- ms.topic: upgrade-and-migration-article. Repo: MicrosoftDocs/memdocs-pr.

**1b. Setup migration guide.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/setup-migration. The H1 is "Migration guide: Set up or move to Microsoft Intune", not "Deployment guide".
- Order: Yes. It has branches per starting point (no MDM, third-party MDM, ConfigMgr options 1–4, GPO, Basic Mobility, tenant-to-tenant). The third-party MDM branch is ordered: set MDM authority, then app protection, then unenroll, then CA blocking until enrolled, then a compliance baseline, then enroll.
- Prerequisites: Yes ("Before you begin").
- Dependencies: devices must leave the old MDM before Intune enrollment. Use app protection policies to cover the gap while devices are unenrolled.
- ms.topic: upgrade-and-migration-article. Repo: memdocs-pr.

**1c. Step 1: Set up Microsoft Intune.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/deploy-setup-step-1
- Order: Yes, 9 steps: supported configurations, sign up, custom domain, users, groups, licences, roles/RBAC, MDM authority, Company Portal.
- Prerequisites: Yes (review the planning guide).
- Dependencies: each user needs an Intune licence before enrolling. The MDM authority must be set before any device enrolls.
- ms.topic: install-set-up-deploy. Repo: memdocs-pr.

**1d. Enrollment guide for Microsoft Intune.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-enrollment/guide
- Order: Partial. It moves from prerequisites to unenroll/factory reset, then the per-platform guide, then pilot groups.
- Prerequisites: Yes.
- Dependencies: MDM authority set to Intune and licences assigned. Apple platforms need an MDM push certificate. User and device groups should exist before enrollment policies.
- ms.topic: article. Repo: memdocs-pr.

**1e. Step 3: Plan for compliance policies.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/fundamentals/deploy-compliance-step-3. ms.date is 2023-11-22, so it is stale.
- Order: Yes, 3 levels: minimal, enhanced, advanced. Conditional Access and Mobile Threat Defense (MTD) integration sit in Level 3.
- Prerequisites: Implicit. It assumes Steps 1–2 (subscription and app protection) are done.
- Dependencies: create email templates before using the "send email" noncompliance action. A CA "require compliant device" policy consumes Intune compliance state. MTD (including MDE) must be integrated before compliance or CA can use its risk signal.
- ms.topic: how-to. Repo: memdocs-pr.

**2. Windows Autopilot requirements.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/autopilot/requirements. It is still under /autopilot/; /intune/autopilot/requirements returns 404.
- Order: No. Tabs cover software, networking, licensing and configuration.
- Prerequisites: Yes.
- Dependencies: configure Entra automatic MDM enrollment first. Devices must be registered as Autopilot devices. Users still need licences assigned even under M365 suites. Entra company branding is optional.
- ms.topic: article. Repo: memdocs-pr.

**3. Windows Hello for Business: cloud Kerberos trust deployment guide.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/deploy/hybrid-cloud-kerberos-trust. The plan page is .../hello-for-business/deploy/ (concept-article).
- Order: Yes: deploy Entra Kerberos, then configure WHfB policy (Intune settings catalog or GPO), then enroll.
- Prerequisites: Yes (links to the plan page).
- Dependencies: the Entra Kerberos server object must exist before the "cloud trust for on-prem auth" policy. Hybrid deployments require both user and device objects synced by Entra Connect. The "use certificate for on-prem auth" policy must be absent, or certificate trust wins. Each AD site needs enough read-write DCs.
- ms.topic: tutorial. Repo: MicrosoftDocs/windows-docs-pr.

**4a. Microsoft Intune support for Windows LAPS.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/laps/overview
- Order: No.
- Prerequisites: Yes (licensing, directory support, OS builds).
- Dependencies: for Entra-joined devices, turn on LAPS in Entra device settings (or via Graph deviceRegistrationPolicy) before the Intune policy can back up. Hybrid join does not need this. Workplace-joined devices are unsupported. The backup directory must match the join type.
- ms.topic: how-to. Repo: memdocs-pr.

**4b. Windows LAPS in Microsoft Entra ID.** https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/howto-manage-local-admin-passwords
- Order: Yes. Enable the tenant setting first, then configure the client policy with BackupDirectory set to Entra.
- Prerequisites: Yes.
- ms.topic: how-to. Repo: MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs-pr.

**5. Purview deployment models.** Landing page https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/deploymentmodels/ (landing-page, index.yml). Overview at .../depmod-overview (best-practice).
- Secure by default: .../depmod-secure-by-default-intro (the old slug "securebydefault" redirects). Purview IP, DLP and IRM.
  - Order: Yes, 4 steps: default labeling; highest-sensitivity files; whole M365 estate; operate and retroactive actions.
  - Dependencies: Step 1 lists the switches to turn on first: SPO/OneDrive label support, container labels, PDF support, co-authoring, DLP and IRM analytics, IRM indicators, audit, Entra B2B integration. It also stages milestones, starting with a default SharePoint label plus DLP and adding encryption later.
- Other blueprints, each with 3–4 numbered steps:
  - Prevent data leak to shadow AI (Purview, MDCA, Entra Internet Access, Intune): discover with MDCA, block with MDCA, Entra and Intune, then Endpoint DLP and Edge DLP.
  - Secure and govern M365 Copilot agents.
  - DSPM.
  - Lightweight DLP: step 2 extends to endpoints.
  - Reduce false positives.
- Repo for all: MicrosoftDocs/Purview-pr; step pages are best-practice.

**6. Sensitivity labels.**
- Get started: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/get-started-with-sensitivity-labels (get-started).
  - Order: No. It suggests deploying one or two scenarios at a time.
  - Prerequisites: Yes (licensing and permissions).
  - Dependencies: every scenario requires labels to be created and published first.
- SharePoint/OneDrive files: .../sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files (how-to).
  - Opt-in. Until enabled, SPO cannot process label-encrypted files, so DLP, eDiscovery, search and auto-labeling don't work on them. Existing encrypted files must be re-uploaded.
  - Next steps (default library label, auto-labeling) come after enablement.
- Containers: .../sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites (how-to).
  - One-time order: enable group label support in Entra, then run Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
  - The label's unmanaged-device option does nothing without the SharePoint app-enforced-restrictions CA policy.
  - The authentication-context option needs a published CA authentication context.
- Repo: Purview-pr.

**7. DLP.**
- Plan for DLP: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-overview-plan-for-dlp (article).
  - Order: Yes. Planning phases, then deployment: simulation without tips, then simulation with tips, then enforce.
  - Prerequisites: Yes. It points to each location's "Before you begin", for example endpoint and on-prem scanner.
- Endpoint DLP get started: .../endpoint-dlp-getting-started (get-started).
- Device onboarding overview: .../device-onboarding-overview (article).
  - Turn on device monitoring and onboard devices before endpoint policies work.
  - Onboarding is shared with MDE, so already-onboarded devices need no further step. Defender AV real-time protection and behavior monitoring must be on.
  - Servers need Endpoint DLP support switched on separately.
- Repo: Purview-pr.

**8. Audit.**
- Get started with auditing solutions: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-get-started (article).
  - Order: Yes, 6 steps: licensing; permissions; search-query events; Audit Premium for users; retention policies; search.
  - Dependency: Audit Premium needs an E5-class licence plus the Advanced Auditing service plan per user.
- Turn auditing on or off: .../audit-log-enable-disable (how-to).
  - Auditing is off by default for Business Basic, Standard and Premium tenants and for unmanaged trial tenants.
  - Turning it on needs the Exchange Audit Logs role. Events can take hours to appear.
- Repo: Purview-pr.

**9. Insider Risk Management.**
- Get started: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/insider-risk-management-configure (get-started).
  - Order: Yes, 6 steps: permissions (required); audit log (required); analytics (optional); policy prerequisites (recommended); settings and indicators (required); policy (required).
  - Dependencies: audit must be on. Several templates require the HR connector (departing users, risky users). Data-leak templates use DLP policies whose incident reports are set to High severity. Security-violation templates need MDE onboarded with the IRM integration enabled in Defender advanced features. Cloud indicators need the cloud apps connected in Defender first.
- Plan: .../insider-risk-management-plan (article) lists the same template dependencies.
- Repo: Purview-pr.

- I relied on rendered text only; I did not open the individual tabs on the Autopilot page.
- I did not read the "Secure and govern M365 Copilot agents", DSPM and "reduce false positives" step pages.
- No source states an IRM device-indicator dependency on endpoint onboarding; I did not find it in the get-started page.
